source.title: The Tangled Web They Weave: Exploring Neural Representations with Directed Simplicial Complexes

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies higher-order causal relations among neurons in small synthetic MLPs, but does not test any of the specified claim versions about neuron-job shares, explanations, canonical examples, or large-model circuits.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on a proxy for identifying polysemantic neurons, which are included as a related finding under versions ["none"]. Its circuit-discovery comparisons do not measure any of the claim versions. Results cited from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study builds directed simplicial complexes from counterfactual ablations in tiny handcrafted, trained and random ReLU MLPs (7–8 hidden neurons) on a synthetic quadrant task. It neither audits neuron job shares in language models, nor examines InceptionV1 examples, nor builds neuron-level attribution graphs for large models, nor scores explanations against held-out activations. Its polysemanticity discussion is a toy proxy, and it notes that semantic labels depend on the chosen input basis. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors present DSCs as context-dependent descriptions of multi-neuron computation: they recover designed pathways in handcrafted networks and agree with circuit-discovery baselines on representable edges. They leave open whether DSCs identify polysemantic neurons and whether higher-dimensional simplices reflect true higher-order interactions. They also note that trained and random networks give DSCs of comparable size.
record.recipe_differences: The paper constructs filtered directed simplicial complexes using coherent counterfactual ablations in small ReLU MLPs; it does not use the neuron-explanation audit or held-out activation scoring methods in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to input distribution and selection tolerance, sample size, relevance margin, test level, multiple-testing correction, and numerical integration step.

fits_no_version.finding: In the handcrafted polysemantic [2,3,4,4] network, the Q4 neuron n7 belongs to the most maximal simplices (14). The six neurons that mix both coordinates belong to 2–7 each.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Participation in counterfactual-ablation simplices does not identify designed polysemantic neurons in a toy MLP; polysemanticity labels depend on the chosen feature basis.

fits_no_version.finding: The 1-skeleton's forward-adjacent edges agree with ACDC, EAP and EAP-IG circuits in 26 of 32 comparisons, with mean AUC 0.86 (minimum 0.65), on small MLPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron-level causal edges in tiny MLPs agree with standard circuit-discovery methods on representable edges. This is not large-model attribution graphs, so it does not bear on V5.

record.problems: Evidence is confined to small ReLU MLPs on a synthetic quadrant-classification task. The authors note that semantic assignments depend on the choice of input features, that their polysemantic-neuron identification question remains open, and that their multiple-testing error rate is not controlled jointly across dimensions, input sets, and networks.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported outcomes directly measure a claim version. Circuit-discovery comparisons concern agreement on representable edges, not the specified neuron-job or explanation claims.

untested.parts: Other dense and mixture-of-experts language models; scale up to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron; pose as a shared feature; recursive generalization versus superposition.
Effects of architecture, regularization and tools on interpretable-neuron share; InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Attribution graphs from a large model's own neurons versus replacement models and their reconstruction error.
Explanations that fit activating examples but fail to predict firing.
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The study shares only the vocabulary of polysemanticity and superposition with the claim. The author stresses that whether a neuron counts as monosemantic depends on the chosen input basis; a 45° rotation swaps the readings of the two networks. This is a conceptual point near V3/V4, but it is not a test of either.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B pole-level audit shares and explanation testing on held-out activations.
Other language models, dense or mixture-of-experts models, and scaling to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Architecture, regularization, and tool effects on interpretable-neuron shares, including the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Attribution graphs from a large model's own neurons and reconstruction error or replacement-model comparisons.
Whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict firing on new examples.
Automated explanation scores based on simulated activations on new text.

rows.subject: handcrafted [2, 3, 4, 4] polysemantic network
rows.operation_detail: Counted each neuron's participation in maximal simplices across the one-hot input complexes.

conditions.value: one-hot inputs for Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4

rows.value: n7 belonged to 14 maximal simplices across the four complexes; each of the six neurons that mix both coordinates belonged to 2 to 7.
rows.note: The authors state that simplex participation did not identify the polysemantic neurons; n7 represents Q4 in this network.
rows.check: The row reports how many maximal simplices each neuron joins in a handcrafted toy network. That is a property of the DSC method, not a share of interpretable neurons or an explanation score, so it bears on no version. The state 'observed' has no meaning against any version; set it to cannot_determine. The value is read correctly (14 for n7 versus 2–7 for each of the six mixing neurons, Appendix G.1).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
